f-prose.$comment:
REVISION 10. Fallbacks widened for cross-device viewing. The design
machine still resolves Constantia, Segoe UI and Ink Free, so nothing
changes here; these only matter when a file is opened on a Mac, an
iPhone or an Android device, which now happens because the prototype is
shared. Georgia is the workhorse fallback and is on essentially
everything. Bundled Lora, Source Sans 3 and Caveat provide deterministic fallbacks
when the approved Windows faces are absent. See EXPORT-HANDOFF.md.

space.$comment: ---- 1.3 SPACE. Nine steps, tied to the 14px graph module. ------------

s6.$description: THE MODULE. the page gutter and the standard inner padding.

gut.$comment:
REVISION 18. THE PAGE GUTTER IS A TOKEN, NOT A LITERAL STEP.
Every object that sits against the edge of the page took --s6 directly:
the masthead, the destination row, the sheet, the glance line, the total,
the notice, the card, the progress bar, the calendar, the composer, the
action bar, the stack, the empty state, the panel and the footer. On
mobile the page gutter and the module are the same 14px, so writing --s6
was harmless and read as correct.
It is not correct. The gutter is the paper margin and the module is the
graph. They agree at 390 by coincidence, and tablet is where they stop
agreeing: the page becomes a defined object and needs a real margin
around it while the module stays 14px forever.
--gut is --s6 at mobile, so every Stage 3 file renders byte-identically.
Verified by pixel diff, not by reading.

mod.$comment: Fixed dimensions. Not part of the scale, not interchangeable with it.
mod.$description: the graph module. same number as --s6, deliberately.

tcol.$description: the time column, and the date column on Timeline

tap.$description: the minimum tap target. a floor, never a height to design to.

ctl.$description: the record control, and the composer field

safe-t.$comment:
REVISION 47. FOUR NATIVE DIMENSIONS, FOR SECTION 6. They are declared here
with --rail, --tcol, --tap and --ctl because they are the same kind of
object: a fixed dimension that is not part of the spacing scale and is not
interchangeable with it. They are unused on the three web platforms,
exactly as --page-w is unused below the tablet threshold.
ALL FOUR ARE APPLE'S OWN NUMBERS, NOT DERIVED BY THIS PROJECT, because a
native pass that invents its own furniture heights is a wrapper with
opinions. In a real build the two safe areas are env() values and are
never typed; they are typed here because a comp has no device to ask.
ONE OF THEM WAS ALREADY IN THIS FILE. --tap has been 44px since the Stage 2
lock, chosen off WCAG, and iOS specifies 44pt for the same thing. The
accessibility floor this project has built to for three platforms is the
native platform's own number, so nothing had to move to meet it.
safe-t.$description:
the status bar. iPhone 12/13/14 class, 390x844.
PRODUCTION: env(safe-area-inset-top).

tabh.$description:
the UITabBar item row, above the home indicator. The bar's
total height is --tabh + --safe-b, which is 83.

navh.$description:
the COLLAPSED navigation bar, once the large title has gone.
The same number as --tap, and that is a coincidence rather
than a derivation: one is a floor and one is a bar height.

page-w.$description:
REVISION 19. The width of the page at tablet and above.
EXACTLY 40 GRAPH MODULES, so the ruling lands on the
page's own edge instead of being cut mid-square. Unused
below the tablet threshold, where the page is the
viewport and has no width of its own.

title-w.$description: REVISION 33 and 45. The desktop title block: the width of the column the masthead takes at 1440, which the rail and the page are welded to. The website preview lets it grow from 360 to 396 by redefining this token on its desktop shell (it was --website-sidebar).

chat-w.$description: v4 C2: Ask's chat column, shared by the head row, the thread and the composer: 760px up to about a 1310px window, then growing with it to 1120px.

chat-answer.$description: v4 C2: the answer bubble's widest, about 90 characters a line at 840px.

chat-you.$description: v4 C2: your message bubble's widest.

leaf-w.$description: v4 C3: a booklet leaf's widest below desktop (one leaf at a time); the spread on desktop is two leaves of the column's width.

leaf-h.$description: v4 C3: a booklet leaf's least height, so the leaves of a booklet turn at one size whatever they say.

r.$description: everything. controls included. paper does not round.

rule.$comment: ---- 1.5 RULE. One weight, and one exception. ----------------------

w.$description:
every rule in the product is 1px, except --w-alert, --w-quote and --w-focus.
rules are told apart by colour and style, not by thickness.

w-alert.$description: a second weight for a refused value only (the invalid field's border), always in --action-delete. Decision 2026-10-11.

w-focus.$description: a focused input box: its own border drawn at 2px in --block, inward, in place of a ring outside it (which covered what sat under the box, e.g. Forgot your password). v4 round 10, decision 2026-10-29.

w-quote.$description: the other second weight: the quotation rule beside the user's own words (an answer's entries used, v4 C2; the excerpt's until it retired), in --rule. Decision 2026-10-11.

w-dash.$description: v4 C2: the third named weight: the dashed edge of an answer the journal could not give (Ask's can't answer), in --rule-2. Decision 2026-10-25.

elev.$description:
no box-shadow on any product surface, at any state.
hierarchy comes from rules, fills and leading. paper does
not float. the only shadow in this project is on .device,
which is presentation furniture and does not ship.
v4 C1 (DESIGN.md 2026-10-23) makes the one exception, on the Timeline: the
search pill while it floats over the list, its found line, and the calendar
sheet that hangs from the date. Nothing else floats.
v4 C3 (DESIGN.md 2026-10-28) gives paper its one lift: the Reflections booklet on the table (--elev-paper).

elev-pill.$description: v4 C1: the search pill's lift while it floats over the list (stuck), and its found line's.

elev-glow.$description: v4 C1: the pill's own soft glow (e-pill-glow, gentler): it softens the writing at the pill's edge only.

elev-glow-s.$description: v4 C1: the found line's glow under the stuck pill, a size down from the pill's.

elev-sheet.$description: v4 C1: the calendar sheet hanging from the date over what is under it.

elev-paper.$description: v4 C3: the Reflections booklet lifting off the table, a contact shadow and a soft wide one. The first paper elevation; nothing else on paper floats.

mood-good-ground.$description: v4 C1: the mood graph's ground when the week's average mood is good (DESIGN.md 2026-10-23, the area rule).

mood-hard-ground.$description: v4 C1: the mood graph's ground when the week's average mood is hard (DESIGN.md 2026-10-23, the area rule).

mood-light-wash.$description: v4 C1: the jump arrival's wash on a light day (30% hurt reading).

mood-good-wash.$description: v4 C1: the jump arrival's wash on a good day (30% hurt reading).

mood-even-wash.$description: v4 C1: the jump arrival's wash on a even day (30% hurt reading).

motion.$comment: C3 glide. Every duration is its own object's distance over a fixed speed; see lock.css 3.10 and direction-lock.md 7.7. Scoped to the shell module (.aj-l-shell; .app until 2026-10-13), so a shell its render draws carries them too.

g-date.$description:
was 440, derived from Today's date. 500 is derived from
the WIDEST date in the product, 07-you's 225.2px at 15
characters. See WHAT THE EXTENSION FORCED above.

g-type.$description:
was 800, derived from the glance line's 47 characters.
THE PRINTED LINE IS NOW BOTH OBJECTS AND THE LONGEST OF
THEM IS THE TOTAL, at 48. Same rule as --g-date: derive
from the widest instance in the product, not from
Today's. 48 x 16.667 = 800.0ms is the floor at one
character a frame, so 820 clears it at 1.025 frames a
character where 800 would sit exactly on it.
.total was removed on 2026-10-12 (v4 drops Timeline totals); the value stays.

g-wave.$description:
the row wave at 390 and 834. Desktop overrides it below,
because its widest row is 788.3px and breaks the ceiling.

gc-c1.$description: v4 C1: the one ease-in-out curve of the Timeline's pill, mood panel, calendar, frame and wash.

g-panel.$description: v4 C1: the search pill's morph and the mood panel's open and close.

g-cal.$description: v4 C1: the calendar unrolling from the date. It travels about 1.55 times the mood panel's distance, so its top speed stays near the panel's (650 felt slow).

g-frame.$description: v4 C1: the arrival frame drawn round the day.

g-wash.$description: v4 C1: the arrival wash passing through the day, in from the left and out to the right, with no hold.

g-wash-step.$description: v4 C1: each further row of the day starts its wash this much after the one above.

gc-drawer-in.$description: v4 C2: Ask's drawers (History, Bookmarks) arriving: a sharp start that settles.

g-drawer-in.$description: v4 C2: a drawer opening, and the dim fading in.

gc-drawer-out.$description: v4 C2: a drawer leaving, an ease-out.

g-drawer-out.$description: v4 C2: a drawer closing, and the dim fading with it.

g-shimmer.$description: v4 C2: one loop of the skeleton's shimmer, a lighter band sweeping left to right across every bone at once.

g-turn.$description: v4 C3: a booklet leaf turning over the spine (rotateY -96deg from its left edge, on --gc) and fading as it goes.

g-lean.$description: v4 C4: the overview's chevron leaning toward where it leads on hover and focus (on --gc-rise), and its underline turning solid with it.

g-lean-back.$description: v4 C4: the overview's chevron settling back when hover or focus leaves (on --gc-rise).

g-lean-x.$description: v4 C4: how far the overview's chevron leans and nudges.

g-nudge.$description: v4 C4: the overview's chevron nudging out and back once when a new reflection is first shown (on --gc).

g-nudge-wait.$description: v4 C4: the wait before the nudge, so it comes after the page has arrived.

g-lift.$description: v4 C5: one loop of the upload arrow lifting 2px and settling while an unsent entry or memo sends (on --gc, looping until it is uploaded). Reduced motion: still; the words say it.

skeleton.$comment: ---- v4 C2: the loading skeleton (Ask). Derived from the roles, not new colours. ----

bone.$description: a bone: the shape of words, a bubble's line or a tool still to come.

bone-shine.$description: the shimmer's lighter band sweeping across the bones.
